Simple and Traditional Ford Crown Victoria ST Comes From the Digital Realm, Probably Rocks Turbo V6
11 photos
Photo: jlord8 / Instagram
Currently, the big Detroit Three don’t make nearly as many passenger cars as they used to back in the day. Ford has the Mustang, Chevy has the C8 Corvette, and Dodge has the Charger. Oh, and Cadillac has the CT5 because the smaller CT4 is going bust.
The Ford Motor Company banks on the credibility of the iconic Mustang pony car and sells both coupe and convertible variants with EcoBoost and V8 power under the hood. GM thinks that Chevrolet only needs the high-performance Corvette in its life, with all versions powered by V8s and again with coupe or convertible body styles. There’s also the dying CT4 compact executive sedan and the larger CT5, which is getting a new generation for the Cadillac roster.
As for Stellantis, they sell the traditional Dodge Charger in both sedan and coupe form as the Challenger has been retired, and offer both EV and inline-six turbo Hurricane powertrains. In the near future, GM is moving faster than the others with a reported next-gen Cadillac CT5 sharing its underpinnings with the reborn Chevy Camaro and even a new Buick sedan!
But over at Ford, all is quiet on the passenger car front, except for the occasional hints that the S650 Mustang could get a four-door sedan body style to compete with the larger Dodge Charger more directly. Alas, a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI has other plans.
Jim, a virtual artist known as " jlord8 " on social media, loves messing around with all things CGI from the automotive realm, and he dreams of a Ford car – once again imagining the potential return of the iconic Crown Victoria.
The latter was a nameplate that ran from 1992 through 2012 as a full-size, traditional sedan across two generations. It replaced the Ford LTD Crown Victoria and was positioned above the Ford Taurus as the largest sedan in North America, twinned with the Mercury Grand Marquis. It was especially famous due to the extensive use for law enforcement via the Crown Victoria Police Interceptor version, as well as the long-wheelbase Crown Victoria sedan sold to the taxi cab fleets.
Over the years, this pixel master has attempted on many occasions to bring back the Ford Crown Victoria nameplate, and his latest unofficial, hypothetical design project joins the roster with the looks of a traditional sedan packing Ford’s current ST design language. As such, we feel that it’s only appropriate for a matching powertrain – perhaps the one from the 2027 Ford Explorer ST, a 385-hp and 415 lb-ft of torque 3.0L EcoBoost V6 mill? So, what do you think – yay or nay? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Jim (@jlord8)
